title: A manuscript in disguise
text: "It's a medieval text by an unknown author, supposedly a follower of Charvaka… Ancient texts do that on purpose. They camouflage themselves in their decayed covers, afraid of being discovered."
source: The Professor, on the day Dvij wakes

title: A work of fools
text: Charvaka denounced the grand ashvamedha horse sacrifice, calling it "a work of fools", and was ostracised for it. His works were destroyed, or so the world believes.
source: The Professor's history of the valley

title: Not destroyed
text: "Charvaka's texts were not destroyed. I have discovered some in this very valley." And then, almost lightly: "Do you think that puts me under grave peril?"

match: Charvakas had made it their home
title: Vidgati's shrine
text: Half way up Mount Dronagiri, on a plateau cut by a vanished Buddhist settlement: a shrine to Vidgati, a Charvaka semi-saint. "The followers of Charvaka's philosophy had made this place their home."

title: While life is yours
text: "While life is yours, live joyously." The round-nosed man's greeting is the best-known line attributed to the Charvakas (yāvaj jīvet sukhaṁ jīvet), and they live by it.
